scope_review: The learner drives or prepares a normal passenger car; no specialist vehicle operating rules.
learning_objective: Identify both stopped approach directions from an officer’s horizontal arms
novelty_review: The older situation_officer_stop_over_green tests precedence over a green light. This corrected item tests interpreting the gesture and the opposite approach; no longer asks which instruction takes precedence.
scenario: Face-on officer at a quiet four-way French junction with both arms held horizontally; front and rear approaches visible, no traffic lights.
image_prompt: Use case: photorealistic-natural. Create one original realistic French driving-theory scene photograph, landscape 16:9. Driver-eye view from a stationary ordinary left-hand-drive passenger car at a quiet four-way urban junction in France. A uniformed traffic police officer is clearly visible facing directly toward our car, standing about seven metres ahead at the centre of the intersection. Officer's full body occupies approximately half the image height, with BOTH arms straight and extended HORIZONTALLY at shoulder height to the officer's left and right, forming a clear T shape. Both hands open with five natural fingers each, palms facing the approaching driver. Both shoulders level, two normal arms and two normal hands, feet together. Fluorescent yellow vest over dark uniform. Clear daytime natural photo. Simple stone buildings and pavements well behind the officer. Road extends straight behind the officer to show the opposite approach. No other people or moving vehicles at this instant. No traffic lights, road signs, readable text, logos, number plates, unnecessary lane markings or gauges. Small dashboard rim at bottom, full scene and physically plausible perspective. No quiz panel, answer choices, annotations, highlighted solution, collage, or watermark. The learning question will ask which approaching directions must stop for the two horizontally extended arms; the gesture must be unmistakable at phone size.

fr.question_text: L’agent maintient ses deux bras tendus horizontalement. Quels conducteurs son geste oblige-t-il à s’arrêter ?
fr.answer_a: Seulement ceux qui arrivent de sa gauche.
fr.answer_b: Seulement ceux qui arrivent de sa droite.
fr.answer_c: Uniquement ceux qui voient son visage.
fr.answer_d: Ceux qui arrivent face à lui ou dans son dos.
fr.explanation: Les bras tendus horizontalement imposent l’arrêt aux usagers venant des directions qui coupent l’axe des bras. Les conducteurs placés face à l’agent et ceux arrivant dans son dos doivent donc s’arrêter. Il faut observer sa position et son geste.

en.question_text: The officer holds both arms out horizontally. Which approaching drivers does this signal require to stop?
en.answer_a: Only drivers approaching from the officer’s left.
en.answer_b: Only drivers approaching from the officer’s right.
en.answer_c: Only drivers who can see the officer’s face.
en.answer_d: Drivers approaching the officer from the front or from behind.
en.explanation: Arms held horizontally stop road users approaching from directions that cross the line of the arms. Drivers facing the officer and those approaching from behind the officer must therefore stop. Observe both the officer’s position and gesture.

Four options, D only, FR/EN explanations agree with Vienna Convention article 6(3)(b). Existing stable question key retained as a historical identifier.
